method: The existing local Mineral boundary-fit transform was applied. The PDF /VP geographic transform and the source raster PGW were not used for output coordinates.
page_to_wgs84: lon = lon_center + lon_deg_per_1000_page_pt * (page_x - page_x_center) / 1000; lat = lat_center + lat_deg_per_1000_page_pt * (page_y - page_y_center) / 1000
country_mask: Fixed Nigeria Admin-0 polygon in shapefiles/nigeria_admin0/; applied to M2 raster classes to restrict output to Nigeria.
class_method: Six filled-area classes matched to the map legend swatch RGB values, closed across small hatch/overprint gaps, and polygonized. Gneiss-Migmatite-Granite Complex was derived as the residual land polygon within the Nigeria mask after the six color-class polygons and mapped blue water were removed.

pegmatite_adjustment.pegmatite_coordinate_adjustment: For each source point, invert the source /VP affine to recover PDF page x/y, then apply the local Mineral boundary-fit affine. The source /VP longitude/latitude remain in vp_lon/vp_lat.

limitations: M2 geology is raster-only in the Mineral PDF. Polygon boundaries are approximate at about 0.68 km per source raster pixel.
Mineral symbols and text are burned into the source raster; small overprint gaps were generalized during polygonization.
The Gneiss-Migmatite-Granite Complex is a residual white class and is lower confidence than the color-matched classes.
Pegmatite geometries are locations of 23 printed P marks, not survey positions or mapped pegmatite body polygons.
Sand Bars appears as a separate line symbol in the legend; it was not converted to a polygon or included in the requested seven area classes.
Features are restricted to the fixed Admin-0 reference polygon for M2 polygonization; G1-G5 source geometries were not clipped.
Pegmatite near-locality distances and host-unit attributes are retained from the source extraction and were not recomputed after coordinate adjustment.
